Tech ethicist Tristan Harris joins the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 1558. Harris, a former Google design thinker, became the best-known critic of addictive app design, arguing that phones are built to capture minds. His warnings reached Congress and a huge Netflix audience.

He explains the tricks feeds use to hold attention, and what they do to mood, politics, and childhood. Rogan asks whether users can fight back or whether the design always wins. The episode is a clear, urgent tour of the attention economy from one of its first defectors, made for an audience that lives on the same apps.
